head: 876a2b0c67dae275c199415752226ed71c9c344f
principle: Evidence never contains a credential value: only SHA-256 prefixes, lengths, PIDs and port ownership. Invalidity is proven by process teardown + file replacement, not by redaction.

previouslyExposed.source: sessionDetails.json snapshot observed at 2026-10-26T13:49:09 (S1 audit exposure; value never printed)

revocationBasis: The MATLAB process that minted the exposed key (pid 7008) has exited; the connector credential lives only in that process, so it cannot authenticate any current server.
The session descriptor no longer carries that value (SHA-256 prefix 852b6e6d... absent; replacement hash differs and has a different length), so no client reading the descriptor can obtain it.
revocationLimits: No positive replay test was possible: the original value was never copied by this project and is no longer readable from disk, so it could not be presented to a live server. Port 31519 is now reused by an unrelated MATLAB process, which is consistent with the old session being gone but is not by itself proof of server-side invalidation.
conclusion.actionTakenByAgent: Rotated by starting a session this run owns (shareMATLABSession rewrote sessionDetails.json at 19:14:53). No external service was called and no credential value was printed or copied.
stillNeedsHumanReview: The 2026-10-17 untracked snapshot artifacts/tmp_probe/session_ready.json still stores a stale apiKey/certificate copy; it is outside git (ignored by .gitignore:1) and provably inert, but was kept rather than deleted because history is not destroyed without approval.
Earlier S1 traces that carried the exposed value remain in history; if that value was ever valid outside loopback, MathWorks-side revocation is not observable from this machine.
